segment_reference_payload.description: Segment's Amazon Lambda destination invokes a specified AWS Lambda function with the full event JSON as the payload. The function name and invocation type are configured in the Segment destination settings. Segment typically uses synchronous invocation (RequestResponse) so that delivery errors are surfaced immediately.
segment_reference_payload.integration_method: AWS Lambda Invoke API via AWS SDK

config_fields.region: AWS region where the Lambda function is deployed
config_fields.roleAddress: IAM Role ARN for cross-account invocation
config_fields.externalId: External ID for STS AssumeRole (confused deputy protection)

lambda_invocation.function_name: Configured in Segment destination settings (function name or ARN)
lambda_invocation.payload_format: Raw event JSON — full Segment event object serialized as JSON bytes

rudderstack_expected_payload.description: RudderStack's Lambda producer wraps the event payload in an inputData struct with a 'payload' string field before passing it to the Produce method. The Produce method extracts the payload string, decodes the destination config (function name, invocation type, optional client context) from the destConfig map, and creates a lambda.InvokeInput for the AWS SDK v2 Lambda Invoke API. The default invocation type is 'Event' (asynchronous/fire-and-forget) rather than Segment's 'RequestResponse' (synchronous).

connection.protocol: AWS SDK v2 HTTP client to Lambda Invoke API

config_fields.IAMRoleARN: IAM role ARN for cross-account invocation via STS AssumeRole
config_fields.ExternalID: External ID for STS AssumeRole (confused deputy protection)

session_config.MaxIdleConnsPerHost: Configurable via Router.LAMBDA.httpMaxIdleConnsPerHost or Router.LAMBDA.noOfWorkers or Router.noOfWorkers (default: 64)

input_data_format.description: Events are wrapped in an inputData struct with a single 'payload' field containing the JSON-serialized event as a string. The Produce method unmarshals the incoming json.RawMessage into this struct before extracting the payload.

aws_api_error.description: Parsed via common.ParseAWSError into HTTP status code, status string, and message; logged with structured fields (statusCode, respStatus, responseMessage)

invocation_type.segment: RequestResponse (synchronous — delivery errors are returned immediately)
invocation_type.rudderstack: Event (asynchronous/fire-and-forget by default — configurable via destination config 'invocationType' field)
invocation_type.parity_gap: Default invocation type differs: Segment defaults to synchronous (RequestResponse), RudderStack defaults to asynchronous (Event). This affects error visibility — synchronous invocations surface Lambda execution errors, while asynchronous invocations return 202 immediately and errors are handled by Lambda's built-in retry/DLQ.

function_name.segment: Configured in destination settings; passed as FunctionName to Lambda Invoke API
function_name.rudderstack: Configured in destination config map under 'lambda' key; decoded via mapstructure.Decode into destinationConfig.Lambda; passed as FunctionName to lambda.InvokeInput
function_name.parity_gap: No functional difference — both pass the function name/ARN to the same AWS Lambda Invoke API field

payload_envelope.segment: Raw event JSON is sent directly as the Lambda payload (Invoke.Payload bytes)
payload_envelope.rudderstack: Event JSON is wrapped in an inputData struct with a 'payload' string field for the Produce method. However, the actual Lambda invocation uses inputData.Payload directly as Invoke.Payload bytes, so the Lambda function receives the same raw event JSON.
payload_envelope.parity_gap: No difference at the Lambda invocation level — the Lambda function receives identical raw event JSON in both cases. The inputData wrapper is an internal transport detail of the RudderStack stream manager Produce method and does not affect the final payload.

client_context.rudderstack: Optional 'clientContext' field in destination config; passed as InvokeInput.ClientContext (Base64-encoded JSON with client-specific data for the Lambda function)
client_context.parity_gap: RudderStack supports an additional ClientContext parameter not commonly used by Segment

event_envelope_fields.segment: Standard Segment event fields: type, event, userId, anonymousId, timestamp, properties/traits, context (with library.name=analytics.js), messageId
event_envelope_fields.rudderstack: Standard RudderStack event fields: type, event, userId, anonymousId, timestamp, properties/traits, context (with library.name=rudder-sdk-js), messageId, plus additional fields: rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt
event_envelope_fields.parity_gap: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to every event payload. The context.library.name identifies the SDK (rudder-sdk-js vs analytics.js). Lambda functions processing events from both platforms must account for these additional fields.

authentication.segment: AWS IAM credentials configured in destination settings (region, role ARN, external ID)
authentication.rudderstack: AWS IAM credentials configured in destination config (Region, IAMRoleARN, ExternalID); uses awsutils.NewSessionConfigForDestination and awsutil.CreateAWSConfig to create AWS SDK v2 config
authentication.parity_gap: No functional difference — both use IAM-based authentication for Lambda invocation. RudderStack additionally configures MaxIdleConnsPerHost for connection pooling.

error_handling.segment: Synchronous invocation surfaces execution errors immediately; retries based on Segment's retry policy
error_handling.rudderstack: AWS API errors parsed via common.ParseAWSError into HTTP status code and message; client faults return 400, server faults return 500; errors logged with structured fields via rudder-go-kit/logger
error_handling.parity_gap: Different error surfacing due to default invocation type difference. Segment's synchronous invocations catch Lambda execution errors; RudderStack's asynchronous invocations rely on AWS Lambda's built-in retry and DLQ mechanisms for execution errors.

destinationConfig.description: Decoded from destConfig map via mapstructure.Decode

fields.invocationType: AWS Lambda invocation type (Event, RequestResponse, DryRun); defaults to 'Event' if empty
fields.clientContext: Optional Base64-encoded JSON client context for the Lambda function; omitted from InvokeInput if empty
fields.lambda: Name or ARN of the target AWS Lambda function to invoke

inputData.description: Unmarshalled from incoming json.RawMessage in the Produce method

fields.payload: JSON string of the full event; passed as Invoke.Payload bytes

aws_session_config.MaxIdleConnsPerHost: Configurable via Router.LAMBDA.httpMaxIdleConnsPerHost or Router.LAMBDA.noOfWorkers or Router.noOfWorkers (default: 64)

critical_gaps.impact: Different error handling semantics — synchronous invocations surface execution errors, asynchronous invocations fire-and-forget
critical_gaps.mitigation: Configure invocationType to 'RequestResponse' in RudderStack destination config for parity

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to event payloads
non_critical_differences.impact: Lambda functions must tolerate additional fields when processing events from RudderStack
Lambda functions that branch on library name must handle both identifiers

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack supports optional ClientContext parameter for Lambda invocations
non_critical_differences.impact: Additional capability — no negative parity impact

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack configures MaxIdleConnsPerHost for the Lambda HTTP client via Router config
non_critical_differences.impact: Performance tuning — no payload parity impact

parity_summary.functional_equivalence: Both platforms invoke the same AWS Lambda Invoke API with the same function name and event JSON payload. The Lambda function receives identical event data (modulo envelope field differences). Authentication uses the same IAM-based mechanism.

notes: AWS Lambda shared stream destination. Segment slug: amazon-lambda. RudderStack package: services/streammanager/lambda/. Both platforms use the AWS Lambda Invoke API to deliver events. The primary parity difference is the default invocation type: Segment uses RequestResponse (synchronous) while RudderStack defaults to Event (asynchronous). The actual event payload delivered to the Lambda function is functionally equivalent, with RudderStack adding rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, and receivedAt envelope fields. Lambda functions should be designed to tolerate these additional fields for cross-platform compatibility.
